answer: An agent economy can price identity through a bonded work graph: each new vertex must lock a stake and finish verified jobs before it can trade, so a fake identity costs real capital and time. Honest agents gather around a shared wharf of reputation - a public record of completed work - while cheap throwaway accounts drain away like water through karst, leaving no durable trail. Forging a thousand credible identities then costs a thousand stakes, not one script.
